# Volatility Farm

> Independent short-term research on stocks in the days after they report earnings - what changed, what the market got right or wrong, and the risks over the next 10-30 days.

Volatility Farm publishes one research report per company shortly after its earnings release, plus site-wide sections tracking an earnings calendar, cross-asset market regimes, and the realised performance of the ideas published here. Reports are informational research, not investment advice.

## Site sections

- [Calendar](https://volatilityfarm.com/#calendar): Upcoming and recent earnings dates for tracked tickers, with expected and realised price-impact statistics around the print.
- [Market Regimes](https://volatilityfarm.com/#regimes): Persistency (mean-reverting vs trending) and volatility (calm vs volatile) regime scatter plots for SP500, inverse volatility, gold, and short/intermediate/long-term bond proxies, traced over the last 30 days.
- [Performance](https://volatilityfarm.com/#performance): Realised performance of the portfolio implied by the published reports, benchmarked against SPX and VTI, with summary metrics (beta, alpha, Sharpe, Calmar, max drawdown, average position duration).
- [Reports archive](https://volatilityfarm.com/#reports): Full chronological list of every published company report.
- [Method](https://volatilityfarm.com/#method): How reports are built - scope-before-data, sourced tables, no investment advice, in-house analytics.
- [About](https://volatilityfarm.com/#about): Who publishes this, coverage, community, and contact.

## Reports

One short-term research report per company, published within a few days of its earnings release. Each covers the print itself, the market reaction, and the risks over the following 10-30 days.

- [NRG Energy, Inc. - 9 Nov 2026](https://volatilityfarm.com/reports/nrg-energy-inc-2026-11-09.htm): Third-quarter 2026 adjusted EPS was $4.68 against ~$3.16 expected, and adjusted EBITDA rose 67% to $2.01B on the LS Power plants bought in January and a hot Texas summer. NRG reaffirmed 2026 guidance, set 2027 at $9.05 a share at the midpoint, and agreed to sell six gas plants (4.9 GW) to LS Power for $4B, funding $3B of buybacks across 2026–27 and $2–3B of debt reduction. The stock closed at $88.29 on 6 Nov, 53.5% below its February high, after falling 13.5% on 4 Nov when a Democratic sweep, including the Texas governorship, hit power stocks. It was indicated ~4% higher before the open on 9 Nov. Over the next 10–30 days a single-digit multiple and an accelerated buyback support it; Texas policy risk, ~$22.8B of net debt and a weak regime weigh on it.
- [TG Therapeutics, Inc. - 9 Nov 2026](https://volatilityfarm.com/reports/tg-therapeutics-inc-2026-11-09.htm): Q3 total revenue of $259.9M beat consensus by 5.9%, but $15.8M of it was a one-off partner milestone and U.S. BRIUMVI grew only 2.2% sequentially, while new guidance of ~$1.0B implies a 12–14% Q4 jump. With the stock 3% off its high, short interest near 28% of float and its Volatility state at the 86th percentile of the past year, over the next 10–30 days the evidence favours a range-bound, two-way tape — company news, not the market, decides the month.
- [Fortis Inc. - 4 Nov 2026](https://volatilityfarm.com/reports/fortis-inc-2026-11-04.htm): A C$32.2bn five-year plan, 7.5% rate-base growth and a 4% dividend raise confirm the thesis, but the stock reached a 52-week high before the release and sits above every converted analyst consensus measure. Over the next 10–30 days the open question is the Arizona Corporation Commission vote on Tucson Electric Power rates, with the share price already at the top of its one-year volatility range.
- [Booking Holdings Inc. - 4 Nov 2026](https://volatilityfarm.com/reports/booking-holdings-inc-2026-11-04.htm): Third-quarter 2026 room nights rose 7% and gross bookings 10%; adjusted revenue grew 9% to $9.79B and adjusted EPS 17% to $4.66, both ahead of consensus. Reported revenue fell 1% because of a $900M FTC-related reduction, part of a $1.0B charge excluded from adjusted figures. The fourth-quarter guide was weak: room nights +1–3% and adjusted EBITDA about flat, as the Middle East conflict, high airfares and European unrest hit October. The stock closed at $155.67, 29.5% below its December high, and was trading near $169 (+8.6%) early on 4 Nov as travel stocks rallied. Over the next 10–30 days a low multiple and heavy buybacks support it; a soft Q4, target cuts and AI-disintermediation fears weigh on it.
- [Keurig Dr Pepper Inc. - 3 Nov 2026](https://volatilityfarm.com/reports/keurig-dr-pepper-inc-2026-11-03.htm): Q3 cleared consensus on sales and earnings, yet the stock gave back about 5% on the day because the beat leaned on a $99 million tariff refund and the legacy EPS outlook was trimmed on softer single-serve coffee. With 99% of daily variance company-specific and its Volatility state at a one-year high, the stock trades on its own story over the next 10–30 days — and that story has just turned from refreshment momentum to coffee-demand doubt.
- [Jazz Pharmaceuticals plc - 3 Nov 2026](https://volatilityfarm.com/reports/jazz-pharmaceuticals-plc-2026-11-03.htm): Third-quarter 2026 revenue was a record $1.24B, up 10% and about 3% above consensus. Xywav grew 12% with 425 net patient adds, oncology rose 34%, and full-year revenue guidance went to $4.775–4.85B from $4.60–4.75B. A pre-announced $754M Actio charge turned the quarter into a $3.88 adjusted loss per share; without it adjusted EPS was $7.15. The stock closed at $214.44, 18% below its August high, and barely moved after hours. Over the next 10–30 days estimate revisions, a new $500M buyback and early Ziihera demand support it, while Takeda's orexin launch in narcolepsy is the risk the market is pricing.
- [Ryman Hospitality Properties, Inc. - 3 Nov 2026](https://volatilityfarm.com/reports/ryman-hospitality-properties-inc-2026-11-03.htm): Third-quarter 2026 revenue was a record $656M, up 10.7% and about 3% above consensus. Same-store RevPAR rose 7.9% on a three-point occupancy gain, adjusted FFO per share was $1.79 against roughly $1.60 expected, and full-year adjusted FFO guidance went to $9.16–9.43 a share from $8.90–9.26. Entertainment was the soft spot, with its EBITDAre guide cut by $3M. The stock closed at $134.90, 1.9% below its July high, and was indicated about 1.7% higher before the open. Over the next 10–30 days target increases and a trending regime support it; a price already at consensus targets and rate-sensitive REIT trading limit how far it can run.
- [Marriott International, Inc. - 2 Nov 2026](https://volatilityfarm.com/reports/marriott-international-inc-2026-11-02.htm): Third-quarter 2026 worldwide RevPAR rose 6.5% against a 3.5–4.0% guide, with US & Canada up 7.4%. Adjusted EPS of $3.02 beat $2.85, gross fees rose 14% and adjusted EBITDA 12%. Full-year RevPAR guidance went to 4.5–5.0% from 3.0–3.5%, adjusted EPS to $12.07–12.14 from $11.64–11.81, and capital return to at least $4.8B. The stock had already risen 12.5% in 30 days to $399.30, and indicated ~$416 before the open (+4%), above its $404 high. Over the next 10–30 days estimate upgrades and a trending regime support it, while a valuation above most targets limits it.
- [Starbucks Corporation - 30 Oct 2026](https://volatilityfarm.com/reports/starbucks-corporation-2026-10-30.htm): Fiscal Q4 2026 global comparable sales rose 7.2% against ~6% expected. US comps rose 7.7%, with transactions up 2.4% after a 0.9% fall a year earlier, and non-GAAP EPS of $0.80 beat $0.71. Revenue of $9.14B (−4%, after China moved to a joint venture) missed ~$9.2B, and International comps rose only 0.9%. FY2027 guidance of $3.15–3.25 non-GAAP EPS sits just above the ~$3.14 consensus, with ~$1B of buybacks. The stock had already risen 12% in 30 days to $105.51, 2.8% below its high, and slipped ~2% after hours. Over the next 10–30 days the holiday launch, Red Cup Day (17 Nov) and post-print estimate changes decide whether it breaks out or gives back the run-up.
- [Reddit, Inc. - 30 Oct 2026](https://volatilityfarm.com/reports/reddit-inc-2026-10-30.htm): Q3 2026 revenue rose 53% to $895M, ahead of the ~$875–886M consensus. Diluted EPS of $1.40 beat $1.33 and the adjusted EBITDA margin reached 45%. But search referral traffic fell "meaningfully", accelerating into October, US daily uniques fell 2% year on year, and Reddit said Q4 daily users could drop by a low-double-digit percentage. The Q4 revenue guide ($1.00–1.03B) sits below the ~$1.04–1.05B consensus. The stock fell from $129.60 to ~$106 after hours. Over the next 10–30 days traffic data and target cuts will decide whether the market looks through a user problem to a pricing story that is still working.
- [Ambev S.A. - 30 Oct 2026](https://volatilityfarm.com/reports/ambev-sa-2026-10-30.htm): Third-quarter 2026 organic revenue rose 7.6% and normalized EBITDA 8.9%, to R$7.27B, about 1.5% below consensus. Normalized profit of R$4.39B (+14.3%) beat on lower financial costs and tax, but Brazil beer volume rose only 0.5% while the industry grew about 4%. Ambev holds R$19.2B of net cash and approved a new buyback of up to 190M shares. The ADR had already fallen 14.2% on 26 Oct after Lula won Brazil's runoff, and closed at $2.67, down 19.1% in four sessions. Over the next 10–30 days the new economic team, the real and the beer excise bill matter more than the quarter.
- [Boston Scientific Corporation - 28 Oct 2026](https://volatilityfarm.com/reports/boston-scientific-corporation-2026-10-28.htm): Q3 2026 sales rose only 1.5% to $5.14B, roughly in line with consensus, after the 25 August cyberattack cost ~300 bps of growth and ~$0.07 of EPS. Adjusted EPS was $0.73, below the company's own $0.80–0.82 guide. Q4 sales are now guided to fall 1–3%, and management expects 2027 to be "the trough", with electrophysiology and WATCHMAN still losing ground. The stock, already down 53% this year, traded ~8% lower at ~$41.64. Over the next 10–30 days the bad news is largely out; the question is whether a 14× multiple and insider buying can hold a floor before there is any growth to point to.
- [The Boeing Company - 28 Oct 2026](https://volatilityfarm.com/reports/boeing-company-2026-10-28.htm): Q3 2026 revenue rose 4% to $24.19B, slightly below the ~$24.37B consensus, and the core loss of $0.34 a share was wider than the ~$0.20 expected. Boeing will hold the 737 at 47 a month into 2027, move 52 a month to the second half of 2027, miss ~500 737 deliveries this year and guide 2027 free cash flow to ~$3B, against roughly $5.5B on the Street. The stock fell 10.7% to $168.18, a 52-week closing low. Over the next 10–30 days the question is whether oversold conditions bring a bounce or target cuts and a weak market-regime map extend the slide.
- [SoFi Technologies, Inc. - 27 Oct 2026](https://volatilityfarm.com/reports/sofi-technologies-inc-2026-10-27.htm): Q3 2026 adjusted net revenue rose 44% to a record $1.37B against a ~$1.26B consensus. Adjusted EPS was $0.18 against $0.17, and SoFi raised 2026 guidance and introduced a 2027 outlook of $6.4B revenue and $0.90 EPS. The stock came into the print at $14.46, down 45% year to date and 55% below its November 2025 high, and traded ~15% higher at ~$16.63 midday. But the Q4 guide is flat on Q3 revenue, and the 2027 plan assumes two rate hikes. Over the next 10–30 days the company has made its case; the FOMC on 28 Oct and the fintech peer prints decide whether a short-covering pop becomes a re-rating.
- [The Procter & Gamble Company - 22 Oct 2026](https://volatilityfarm.com/reports/procter-gamble-company-2026-10-22.htm): Fiscal Q1 2027 organic sales rose 4%, led by 2.4% volume growth, and core EPS of $2.00 beat the $1.88 consensus. P&G kept full-year guidance (core EPS ~$7.00, organic sales +1–3%) even as the commodity headwind grew to $1.4B from $1.0B. But core EPS rose only 1%, core gross margin fell 150 bps, and the stock ran from $145 to $159 in the two weeks before the print. Shares were ~3% higher pre-market at ~$162, above the $162 mean target. Over the next 10–30 days PG trades on its own and against the market; the Colgate, Clorox and Kimberly-Clark reads decide whether the staples rotation holds.
- [Hasbro, Inc. - 20 Oct 2026](https://volatilityfarm.com/reports/hasbro-inc-2026-10-20.htm): Q3 2026 revenue rose 15% to $1.60B and adjusted EPS of $2.90 crushed the $1.85 consensus, with Magic: The Gathering up 34% to over $600M and Wizards earning a 49% margin. Hasbro raised 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance to $1.575–1.625B, above the $1.48B consensus, and doubled its buyback target. But ~$55M of one-off tariff refunds helped, and the full-year revenue guide implies Q4 sales down 4–10%. Shares were ~2% higher pre-market at ~$100.5, after rising 12.5% in a month. Over the next 10–30 days HAS trades on its own news, and the Mattel and holiday-season reads decide whether it reaches its $107 high.
- [General Motors Company - 20 Oct 2026](https://volatilityfarm.com/reports/general-motors-company-2026-10-20.htm): Q3 2026 EBIT-adjusted rose 22% to $4.1B (8.2% margin) and North America earned an 8.7% margin, with adjusted EPS of $3.70 just ahead of $3.63. GM also raised free-cash-flow guidance by $1.5B and authorised a new $20B buyback. But the full-year profit midpoint stayed at $15B and the EPS midpoint ($13.25) sits below the $13.48 consensus; International, China and GM Financial all fell, and US share slipped to 16.1%. Shares were ~8% lower pre-market at ~$76. Over the next 10–30 days GM trades with the market and the auto group; the buyback pace, Ford's print and the rate path decide whether the gap fills.
- [The Travelers Companies, Inc. - 16 Oct 2026](https://volatilityfarm.com/reports/travelers-companies-inc-2026-10-16.htm): Q3 2026 core EPS of $9.18 beat the $7.43 consensus on an 86.8 combined ratio, $234M of favourable reserve development and record investment income, and Travelers bought back $1.5B of stock. But net written premiums were flat (+2% excluding the Canada sale), Business Insurance renewal premium change slowed to 4.1% and personal auto premiums fell 8%. The shares dropped ~5% pre-market and then recovered to ~$386 after the call. Over the next 10–30 days TRV trades with the commercial P&C group and against the market; Chubb, Hartford and Allstate's prints decide whether pricing worries or earnings power win.
- [ManpowerGroup Inc. - 15 Oct 2026](https://volatilityfarm.com/reports/manpowergroup-inc-2026-10-15.htm): Q3 2026 revenue rose 4% to $4.84B (+5% in constant currency) and adjusted EPS of $1.01 matched consensus. But gross margin fell 70 bps to 15.9%, Q4 EPS guidance of $1.03–1.13 sits below the $1.10 consensus, free cash flow was negative and the board named a new CEO from 1 January. Shares were ~19% lower pre-market at ~$42, after doubling between February and August. Over the next 10–30 days the company, not the market, decides the price; analyst resets and the Randstad, Adecco and Kelly prints show whether the gap extends toward $39 or starts to fill.
- [The Progressive Corporation - 14 Oct 2026](https://volatilityfarm.com/reports/progressive-corporation-2026-10-14.htm): Q3 2026 combined ratio was 88.7 (89.5 a year ago) and EPS of $4.37 was about $4.60 before $170M of realised investment losses, above the $4.41 consensus. But net premiums written grew only 4% in the quarter and 2% in September, policies in force growth slowed to 6%, and a $1.3B unrealised bond loss in September cut book value growth. The shares fell ~2.6% pre-market to ~$217, after a 7.5% rally into the print. Over the next 10–30 days PGR trades with the P&C insurers and against the market; the 3 November conference call and Allstate's results decide whether growth fears or underwriting quality win.
- [Fastenal Company - 14 Oct 2026](https://volatilityfarm.com/reports/fastenal-company-2026-10-14.htm): Q3 2026 sales rose 15.5% to $2.46B and EPS of $0.35 beat $0.34, with operating margin up to 21.5%. But gross margin slipped 40 bps to 44.8%, 2026 capex was set at $310–330M (from $231M in 2025), and the shares fell about 4.5% pre-market to ~$49, from near a 52-week high. At 41× trailing earnings and above the $49.45 consensus target, FAST is fully valued. Over the next 10–30 days the stock trades in a quiet, range-bound regime that has historically been followed by gains; the October sales report in early November decides whether the dip is bought.
- [ASML Holding N.V. - 14 Oct 2026](https://volatilityfarm.com/reports/asml-holding-nv-2026-10-14.htm): Q3 2026 sales hit a record €11.7B (+55% YoY) at a record 57.5% gross margin, and Q4 guidance of €14.2–15.2B implies the biggest quarter in the company's history. Management said planned capacity for 2027 and 2028 will not fully meet customer demand, with some customers already asking about 2029–2030 orders. The Amsterdam line opened +2.2% and faded to +0.7%; the ADR was flat pre-market at ~$1,716 after falling 8% in seven sessions. Over the next 10–30 days ASML trades as a semiconductor-sector name (correlation 0.83 with the sector fund, beta 2.2 to the S&P 500), so the late-October chip-equipment and memory prints decide whether the re-rating starts.
- [Johnson & Johnson - 13 Oct 2026](https://volatilityfarm.com/reports/johnson-johnson-2026-10-13.htm): Q3 2026 adjusted EPS of $2.59 beat the $2.53 consensus and sales of $25.40B beat $25.28B, led by Innovative Medicine (+7.7%: Tremfya +68%, Darzalex +15%). Full-year adjusted EPS guidance rose only $0.06 to $11.10, and MedTech grew just 2.5% with international sales +1.5%. A $5.5B talc charge cut GAAP EPS to $0.09. The shares were ~2.5% lower before the open at ~$257, after a 27% gain this year. Over the next 10–30 days J&J trades on a premium multiple (23.8× this year) with little market correlation; peer prints and orthopaedics separation news decide whether the pullback deepens.
- [Adobe Inc. - 13 Oct 2026](https://volatilityfarm.com/reports/adobe-inc-2026-10-13.htm): Five straight beats and a twice-raised outlook have not stopped a 32% slide, because the market is pricing leadership turnover, slowing bookings and AI disruption rather than the quarter. With no earnings print before mid-December and 99.5% of daily variance company-specific, the stock trades on news over the next 10–30 days: a fresh downgrade and a federal labour-program suspension weigh on it, while Adobe MAX on 10–12 November is the one dated event that could change the story.
- [PepsiCo, Inc. - 8 Oct 2026](https://volatilityfarm.com/reports/pepsico-inc-2026-10-08.htm): Q3 2026 beat on revenue and EPS, but full-year core EPS growth guidance was cut to +1–2% from at least +4%, and the stock closed at a 52-week low of $123.73 after nine target cuts in two weeks. The next 10–30 days hinge on whether a cheap valuation holds against a regime backdrop that has rarely favoured PEP, with Coca-Cola and the late-October snack prints as the deciding catalysts.
- [Neogen Corporation - 7 Oct 2026](https://volatilityfarm.com/reports/neogen-corporation-2026-10-07.htm): Neogen beat Q1 FY27 revenue by 9% and nudged FY27 guidance up, trading 11% higher after hours, but with 97% of daily variance company-specific and the stock at its lowest Persistency reading of the year, the next 10–30 days hinge on the Investor Day and the HYCOAT warning-letter response, not the market.
- [Penguin Solutions, Inc. - 7 Oct 2026](https://volatilityfarm.com/reports/penguin-solutions-2026-10-07.htm): Penguin beat on Q4 sales and raised FY27 guidance 40%, but the stock had already risen 24% in 30 sessions with operating cash flow negative for the year, so the next 10–30 days test whether post-print target raises confirm demand before the July pattern of a sharp reversal repeats.
- [NIKE, Inc. - 2 Oct 2026](https://volatilityfarm.com/reports/nike-inc-2026-10-02.htm): After the 1 October close Nike beat on EPS ($0.48 vs $0.43) but missed on revenue ($11.21B, -4%), guiding FY27 adjusted EPS to $1.15-1.35, about 22% below the $1.61 consensus. Shares fell 6.2% after hours to $32.96, a 13-year low, and the next 10-30 days hinge on whether consensus can reset lower into a stock at about 26x guided earnings, in the weakest regime backdrop of any name in this series.
- [Accenture plc - 2 Oct 2026](https://volatilityfarm.com/reports/accenture-plc-2026-10-02.htm): Accenture rose 15.8% on 1 October, its best day on record, after a Q4 beat and $100M+ bookings hit a quarterly record. But the FY27 guide implies only about 0.5-4% organic growth, and the next 10-30 days hold the gain only if analyst upgrades and the October IT-services prints show AI adding to demand rather than deflating it.
- [Jabil Inc. - 1 Oct 2026](https://volatilityfarm.com/reports/jabil-inc-2026-10-01.htm): Jabil beat on every line and guided FY27 above consensus, but the stock fell 10% on a lighter margin guide and crowded AI-linked positioning, with the next 10–30 days testing whether that drop was overdone.
- [Micron Technology, Inc. - 1 Oct 2026](https://volatilityfarm.com/reports/micron-technology-2026-10-01.htm): Micron cleared every bar at seven times run-rate earnings, but the risk for the month is the cycle debate, not the numbers, with the stock trading at about 7× annualised guidance.
- [Carnival Corporation Ltd. - 30 Sep 2026](https://volatilityfarm.com/reports/carnival-corporation-2026-09-30.htm): A beat-and-raise lifted shares 13.4% on record yields and deposits, but with fuel unhedged and a soft Q4 guide, the next 10–30 days hinge on whether crude falls back below $100.
- [Cintas Corporation - 25 Sep 2026](https://volatilityfarm.com/reports/cintas-corporation-2026-09-25.htm): A sixth straight beat-and-raise met an FTC antitrust review of the UniFirst deal, with no fixed timeline and the review itself the single event most likely to reprice the stock.
- [Worthington Enterprises, Inc. - 25 Sep 2026](https://volatilityfarm.com/reports/worthington-enterprises-2026-09-25.htm): A beat on every line met a spike that gave back most of its gain, with the stock in a $56–$62.5 range ahead of the 10 November Investor Day.
- [Brookfield Corporation - 19 Sep 2026](https://volatilityfarm.com/reports/brookfield-corporation-2026-09-19.htm): A 15% earnings beat met an 11% pullback tied to sector, not the company, with the next 10–30 days trading on the alternative-manager complex and a ten-year yield near 5%.
- [Trip.com Group Limited - 16 Sep 2026](https://volatilityfarm.com/reports/tripcom-group-2026-09-16.htm): A 50%-off-highs stock met a $763 million antitrust fine, with 94% of variance idiosyncratic and the next 10–30 days hinging on whether the regulatory chapter is closed.
- [NIO Inc - 2 Sep 2026](https://volatilityfarm.com/reports/nio-inc-2026-09-02.htm): A margin turnaround with 69% revenue growth met missed delivery guidance and a fresh 52-week low, with the September delivery report due around 1 October deciding the next move.
- [Science Applications International Corp - 1 Sep 2026](https://volatilityfarm.com/reports/saic-2026-09-01.htm): A beat and raised guide printed an all-time high before reversing to close up just 1.8%, with book-to-bill at 0.8 and no company catalyst until December.
- [Frontline plc - 28 Aug 2026](https://volatilityfarm.com/reports/frontline-plc-2026-08-28.htm): A record quarter and the largest payout in years lands the shares at a 52-week high, with the next 10–30 days hinging on spot tanker rates against a scheduled dividend drop.
- [J.M. Smucker Company - 26 Aug 2026](https://volatilityfarm.com/reports/jm-smucker-2026-08-26.htm): A blowout beat on coffee pricing and tariff refunds pushed shares to a 52-week high and past the average analyst target, leaving a 99.9% idiosyncratic digestion trade.
- [Tuya Inc - 25 Aug 2026](https://volatilityfarm.com/reports/tuya-inc-2026-08-25.htm): Record premium customers and 16% revenue growth against a near-nil enterprise value, with the earnings catalyst spent and direction now hostage to China-internet sentiment.
- [Walmart Inc - 24 Aug 2026](https://volatilityfarm.com/reports/walmart-inc-2026-08-24.htm): A beat-and-raise quarter met with a 9.2% single-session drop on decelerating comps, leaving a 99.8% idiosyncratic name with no catalyst until November.
- [Alibaba Group Holding Ltd - 24 Aug 2026](https://volatilityfarm.com/reports/alibaba-group-holding-2026-08-24.htm): Cloud revenue accelerating 45% against a 75% profit drop, with a discounted $10.2bn Hong Kong share placement now the swing factor for the next month.
- [Lowe’s Companies Inc - 20 Aug 2026](https://volatilityfarm.com/reports/lowes-companies-inc-2026-08-20.htm): A light revenue miss and a guide cut to the bottom of every range, offset by a cheap multiple and an 87.9% idiosyncratic setup ahead of the September FOMC.
- [Home Depot Inc - 19 Aug 2026](https://volatilityfarm.com/reports/home-depot-inc-2026-08-19.htm): A best-in-class quarter and reaffirmed guidance met a flat tape, with no company catalyst until November and a premium multiple to defend.
- [Baidu Inc - 19 Aug 2026](https://volatilityfarm.com/reports/baidu-inc-2026-08-19.htm): First earnings miss in eight quarters and a close below book value, with AI-cloud growth real but no catalyst before November.
- [BHP Group Limited - 19 Aug 2026](https://volatilityfarm.com/reports/bhp-group-limited-2026-08-19.htm): Record FY2026 EBITDA and the largest dividend in four years, against an FY2027 copper guide cut 11.7% — the next 10–30 days trade as a copper-price instrument.
